messages:
Maya: quick heads-up — noticed a regression in KV reuse across requests after the batching kernel change. p50 token latency up ~12% on longctx runs. flamegraph: https://perf.local/fg/3321 :eyes:
Leon: repro? which workload and config?
Maya: can repro on longctx-eval1 with seq=4096, batch=8. Run: `./bench --workload longctx-eval1 --seq 4096 --batch 8 --kv-ttl 300`. root diff points to cache miss rate spike on prefix keys.
kv-bench-bot: bench results uploaded: /artifacts/bench/3321117777.tar.gz (p50 +12%, cache hit 68% -> 51%).
Rachel: do we still use tenant:user:prompt_hash keying? if so fragmentation maybe from user-level salts. Suggest trying tenant:prompt-prefix only for reuse test.
Samir: +1. Also try sticky-session on router so consecutive reqs from same session prefer same shard; we saw reuse increase in past tests.
Maya: tried tenant:prompt-prefix -> hit rate 62%, latency down 6% vs regression. But memory growth looks worse (kv pages +18% over 10k reqs). suspect evictions causing page churn.
Leon: can you paste the cache-key composition and TTLs?
Maya: `key = f"{tenant}:{prefix_hash}:{session_salt}"` TTLs default 300s, eviction LRU-ish with slab compaction. suspect session_salt causes low cross-request reuse.
Rachel: maybe derive session_salt only for auth-sensitive tokens, not for prefix KV. We can whitelist prefix keys via a key-role header so they don't use session_salt.
Samir: proposal: change key derivation to drop session_salt for first N tokens and add a dynamic TTL ramp (short -> longer as prefix stabilizes). Run A/B at 10% traffic.
Maya: will run A/B tomorrow. Also will capture kernel selection profile while A/B is live; if numbers don't improve we may rollback batching kernel change. Filed: https://issues/RED-1291
Leon: ping me when you have bench logs and flamegraphs. I'll run a kernel-level profiler to confirm interaction between batching path and KV page faults.
Maya: thanks — will post results in this thread. :thumbsup:
